newsitem.title: UK: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest-June 11.
newsitem.headline: Emerging Europe Advertising & Media Digest-June 11.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on
Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name
Products and Markets
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

-- The Russian State Duma Committee on Economic Policy is considering a number of amendments to its advertising bill. A parliamentary debate on limiting advertising time on TV is expected. (Kommersant - Daily, June 6, 1997)
-- A proposed ban on alcohol and tobacco televison advertising in Georgia within the CIS has been heavily criticised by TV companies because it will substantially effect their income.
(Sakartvelos Respublika, June 5, 1997)
-- The ad most liked by Czech TV viewers in April was for Pepsi, a survey from researchers Median showed. (Lidove Noviny, June 6, 1997)

-- Polish copper conglomerate KGHM Polska Miedz, will launch a TV, radio and press advertising campaign to publicise its privatisation. The campaign has been produced by the ITI McCann-Erickson advertising agency.(Rzeczpospolita, June 2, 1997)
-- Polish housewives watch around 230 TV commercials a week, reflecting the average in the European Union, Piotr Gawel, president of advertising agency Ammirati Puris Lintas, said.
(Rzeczpospolita, June 2, 1997)
-- According to research from ANR Praha, the top 10 advertisers on Czech television stations in April included L'Oreal and Moulinex. (Strategie News, May 28 - June 4, 1997)
-- Poland plans to launch a foreign investment and export promotion agency, the treasury ministry's state secretary Janusz Kaczurba said. (Rzeczpospolita, June 2, 1997)

-- The Hungarian marketing association Magyar Marketing Szovetseg will hold its seventh international marketing conference between November 20-21. The conference will cover Central and Eastern European consumer markets, trends and new marketing methods. (Vilaggazdasag, May 30, 1997)
-- The second Russian festival of advertising photos was sponsored by ad agency Premier SV agency. (Sevodnya, June 5, 1997).
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- Ceska Televize was fined one million crowns ($31,300) by the Czech Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting for breaking the law on broadcasting advertisements. That included a 250,000-crown fine for exceeding the maximum limit of commercials and a 750,000-crown for broadcasting unscheduled commercials during sports broadcasts. (Lidove Noviny, June 4, 1997)

-- The Hungarian national radio and television body ORTT has finalised the tender for operating two commercial radio channels. Companies have 90 days beginning June 10 to bid for the Danubius radio channel and another commercial radio channel.
Broadcasting rights will cost 3.0 billion forints ($16.3 million) plus tax. (Vilaggazdasag, May 30, 1997) *********

-- About 500,000 Poles have access to the Internet, with 42.7 percent of that number accessing the World Wide Web from school or university and 37.6 percent using the Internet at work, according to a survey by the Estymator market research firm.(Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, June 2, 1997)

-- The five-year project to measure Czech television viewing by using so-called "peoplemeters" began on schedule on June 1, despite technical problems. Nova Television, Ceska Televize, Prima Television and the organiser of the project, Taylor Nelson AGB Media Facts, are discussing how to overcome the problems.
The project has a five-year budget of 300 million crowns.
(Lidove Noviny, June 3, 1997)

-- The average amount of time people spend listening to the Polish Radio Zet FM station grew to 46 minutes in the first quarter of the 1997 from 23 minutes in the year-earlier period, according to a survey by the SMG/KRC market research firm.
(Gazeta Wyborcza, June 2, 1997)

-- Consumers in Central and Eastern Europe want to watch more locally-made programmes on TV but are prevented from getting them because of the high costs of making programmes. There's huge business potential for foreign investors in buying commercial channels. (Vilaggazdasag, June 4, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
-- McDonald's operates 74 fast food chain outlets in 33 cities across Poland. The chain has invested $73 million in development in the last five years.(Dziennik Praw i Gospodarki, June 4, 1997)

-- Brewer Plzensky Prazdroj in the Czech Republic has increased the price of its premium beer, Pilsner Urquell, to differentiate it from what it regards as inferior brands. By the year 2000 it wants to increase its current 25-percent share of the market share to 40 percent. (Hospodarske Noviny, June 2, 1997)
-- Car maker Daewoo Motor Poland says it plans to increase production of the Tico model to 6,000 cars a month.(Zycie, June 3, 1997)

-- Tesco, the British supermarket chain, plans to expand in Eastern Europe. It has gained a stake in Global Rt and plans to set up a store in the Bulgarian city of Nyiregyhaza. (Napi Gazdasag, May 30, 1997)
-- Computer company Novell has a 60-percent share of Poland's networking software market. The company hopes to increase sales by up to 25 percent in 1997. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, June 4, 1997)
-- Opel Hungary will soon be producing a new car model at its factory in Szentgotthard. (Napi Gazdasag, June 3, 1997)

-- Confectionery maker Cadbury Poland says it has 4.4 percent of the chocolate bar market in Poland and an 8.8-percent share of the market for chocolate-covered wafers. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, June 4, 1997)
-- The Naleczowianka mineral water company, co-owned by Nestle, has launched a Polish bottling operation which cost $7.3 million to build. (Dziennik Praw i Gospodarki, June 4, 1997)
